This starts a process in the banking system which communicates with the agency in the background.

After the scoring result is determined, the information is sent back to the banking process.
The banking process displays a message to the clerk when he receives information about the delay to check again later.
As soon as the result arrives, it can be seen at the frontend.

result.process_description:
The sales clerks in a bank can use their software frontend to receive the credit-scoring for a certain customer. 
This starts a process in the banking system which communicates with the agency in the background. 
This process sends a scoring request to the agency right after the beginning. 
Then, the Agency does a first quick scoring (level 1). 
This will often lead to an immediate result which is then returned directly to the banking system within seconds. 
The banking process presents the result to the clerk sitting at the frontend. 
Sometimes the scoring cannot be determined immediately and takes longer. 
In this case the agency informs the banking process of the delay and then starts the level 2 scoring (which can take up to a couple of minutes). 
After the scoring result is determined, the information is sent back to the banking process. 
The banking process displays a message to the clerk when he receives information about the delay to check again later. 
As soon as the result arrives, it can be seen at the frontend.

result.rule: Direct each message flow from sender to receiver. Its endpoints must belong to different pools and be valid interaction nodes.
Use bpmn:sendTask or bpmn:receiveTask when sending or waiting for a message is itself the modeled unit of work.
Several unconditional outgoing flows from one activity can all proceed. Use a gateway when the description requires a decision or synchronization.

Give every process and every expanded subProcess its own explicit start event and end event. A trigger that occurs after the main flow (for example later feedback or a return) is joined to the main flow by a gateway, or modeled as an event subprocess or a separate process.
Distinguish message tasks from message events: a task models performed work; an event models a message occurrence affecting flow.
Represent each modeled internal workflow with bpmn:process. Use isExecutable=false unless execution-ready behavior is explicitly required and fully specified.

result.rule: When the description says an actor sends requests to several external parties asking for proposals, and then, in a separate step, says that the actor selects one of those parties, so the selection depends on the proposals received: Model the selection as its own bpmn:task, labeled with the selection action the description names, placed on the sequence flow after the task that sends the requests and before any gateway or activity that depends on the selection. Do not merge the selection into the request task and do not omit it, even when the description states the selection in a separate sentence or treats it as a consequence of the requests.

When the description says a decision leads to one of two alternatives, where one alternative is a concrete action performed by a party and is followed by further described actions, or where the other alternative sends the work back so that an earlier action must be performed again: Model every described action on those branches, including the action that follows an approval or confirmation outcome and the action repeated after a return, as its own bpmn:task on the sequence flow that the description orders. Connect the return as a sequence flow back to the earlier task or gateway. Do not omit these actions, and do not replace them with a subProcess or with an end event.

When the description says an actor asks several outside parties for offers and then selects one of them, and it does not describe those outside parties as doing anything in the process after they give their offers: Model the request to the outside parties as one send task in the actor's own lane. Do not add a pool for those parties, a message flow to them, or a receiving participant. Model the selection of one offer as one task in the same actor lane, with the next action the description attributes to that selection (for example, placing the order) included in that task when the description states them together. Do not add a separate user task or gateway for the selection.

When the description says the process begins when an external party uses one of several alternative channels (for example, two different ways of placing the same order), and each channel is described as a separate way of performing that start action: Model each alternative channel as its own task performed by the external party, one task per channel, with no task that combines them. Connect the channel tasks to an exclusive gateway that merges them before the next step of the process, so that exactly one alternative leads onward.

result.rule: When the description states that the process is started by a participant performing an action of their own, such as submitting or entering information, and that the system then acts on that input: Keep the start event as the process trigger, and model the participant's performed action as a task (user task if it is a manual entry) placed after the start event and before the system tasks that process the input. Do not name the start event after that action or use the start event to stand for the action.

When the description states that the process begins with a participant performing an action that the description itself presents as work carried out by that participant: Model the start as an unlabeled start event followed by a task that performs the described action (a user task when the participant works through a system). Do not put the action into the start event label, since that would drop the performed work from the flow.

When the description says the process begins when a party performs an action of its own (for example, reporting something) and that action is followed by further described steps: Model a start event that carries no work, then a task performed by that party, named with the action the description gives for it. Connect that task by a sequence flow to the next described step. Do not make the party's action itself the start event, and do not drop the action from the model.

When the description states that a participant performs a step itself, such as choosing among options or supplying information, and no external occurrence (a message, signal, timer or condition) is described as the thing the process waits for: Model that step as a task performed by the participant, placed in the sequence where the description places it. Do not model it as an intermediate catch event, because a catch event represents waiting for an occurrence that happens outside the performed work. Reserve intermediate catch events and event-based gateways for waits on messages, signals, timers or conditions.
